desc:
The range of a block of numbers is its largest value minus its smallest value. Slide a window of exactly k elements over nums from left to right and return the sum of the ranges of all nums.length - k + 1 windows.

nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5], k = 3
[3,1,4] range 3    [1,4,1] range 3    [4,1,5] range 4
result = 10
constraints: The answer fits in a signed 32-bit integer
hints: Computing max and min with a loop over each window costs O(n * k).
You need the window maximum and the window minimum at the same time, for every position.

Maintain two monotonic deques of indices: one with decreasing values (front is the maximum) and one with increasing values (front is the minimum). Drop front indices that left the window, then add nums[max front] - nums[min front] to the total.
editorial: Use one deque for the maximum and one for the minimum, both storing indices. For the max deque, before pushing index i pop every back entry whose value is at most nums[i], so values decrease from front to back and the front is the maximum. The min deque is the mirror image. Remove the front of a deque when its index is at most i - k.

Once the first window is complete (i ≥ k - 1), add the difference of the two fronts to the total. Each index enters and leaves each deque at most once, so the time is O(n) and the space O(k). The answer is at most 8,000 * 200,000 = 1.6 * 109, which fits in a 32-bit integer.
